text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Thursday.

LONDON - British blue chips surged to a record high for the third day running, spurred on by a resilient Wall Street and a more relaxed view about interest rates and stock valuations. But many institutional investors remained cautious ahead of key U.S. unemployment figures due on Friday which have the potential to burst both the Dow's and the FTSE's bubble. The FTSE 100 closed 39.2 points higher to 4,399.3.

FRANKFURT - Shares ended bourse trade up on gains fueled by the overnight advance on Wall Street. The 30-share DAX raced off to a new record trading high of 3,426.54 points before ending the day up 52.61 points at 3,417.60 points. In post-bourse trade the Dax stood at 3,396.55.

PARIS - Bolstered by Wall Street's strength and a firm dollar, French stocks ended at a record closing level in high volume. The blue-chip CAC-40 index finished up 32.73 points or 1.23 percent at 2,698.92. But that was below a historic high hit earlier in the day of 2,711.12.

ZURICH - Shares rose over one percent to end for the first time above 4,600 points on the blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI), backed by a firmer dollar and Wall Street gains. Dealers said the Swiss bourse tracked most European markets. SMI ended up 58.1 points at closing high of 4,605.2. The broad SPI added 34.82 points or 1.2 percent to 2,925.65.

TOKYO - The stock market closed lower but the Nikkei average pared its losses and crawled back above the psychologically important 18,000 level. The index had earlier dipped below the key line for the first time in over a month after early gains evaporated. The 225-share Nikkei closed down 232.18 points, or 1.27 percent at 18,041.33.

HONG KONG - Stocks edged to a slightly higher close, chiefly due to a more positive interest rate outlook and demand for local market leader HSBC Holdings. The Hang Seng Index inched ahead 5.60 points to close at 13,416.36 after soaring to a high of 13,568.86 at the start of trade.
SYDNEY - The share market closed stronger but slipped from its early Wall Street-inspired highs as initial buying enthusiasm eased. The All Ordinaries index climbed 14.4 points to 2,447.4.

JOHANNESBURG - Shares ended firmer in quiet trade, boosted by a firm Dow Jones overnight. Golds retraced most morning losses and ended slighlty weaker. Dealers said U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's comments on Wednesday were well received by investors. The overall index ended up 13.8 points to 7,084.2 points, industrials added 29.2 points to 8,278.0 and golds fell 2.6 points to 1,430.1.
